name: Opal-Depths
description: Opal-Depths is an oceanic world whose waters display the play-of-color phenomenon of opal, shifting between milky white, ethereal blue, and flashes of orange-red depending on the angle of observation and the activity of suspended mineral particles. The dense atmosphere traps moisture in perpetual cloud banks that spiral across the surface in slow-moving storm fronts, and the ocean beneath is layered, with distinct temperature and salinity gradients creating visible strata of different colors.

Descending through the water column is like moving through a gemstone made liquid. Each layer has its own character: the surface milky and diffuse, the middle depths clear and blue, the abyssal layer dark and warm from geothermal influence. Flora dominates the ecosystem, vast floating mat-organisms that spread across the surface and trailing root-analogs that descend kilometers into the depths. The air above the ocean is heavy with humidity and a faint floral sweetness.

No intelligent life has developed here, but the plant-dominant ecosystem is one of the most productive in surveyed space, converting sunlight and geothermal energy into biomass at rates that exceed terrestrial forests by an order of magnitude. The floating mat-organisms are colonial superorganisms, each one a genetically unified entity that can span hundreds of square kilometers. How they coordinate growth across such distances without a nervous system remains an open question.

Opal-Depths is a living pharmacy, its flora producing an extraordinary range of biochemical compounds as byproducts of their metabolism. Pharmaceutical companies have begun sampling operations, carefully regulated to prevent damage to the mat-organisms. The dense atmosphere and perpetual storms make surface operations challenging, and the organisms' sensitivity to disruption means that careless harvesting could collapse entire colonial networks. The opalescent waters hold more medicine than has yet been cataloged.
